title: Responses interop observer-adapter for streaming & functioncall fidelity
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Our current Responses compatibility layer exhibits subtle behavioral deltas vs. the OpenAI Responses API when handling streaming deltas, interleaved function call events, and structured output tokens. These deltas lead to downstream SDK users seeing reordered events, truncated function arguments, inconsistent role attribution, and mismatched end-of-stream signals for long-running streams. Goal: build an observer-adapter that records raw runtime events, canonicalizes event sequences into an OpenAI-Responses-shaped stream, and provides configurable degradation policies (best-effort, strict, replayable) to guarantee deterministic behavior for client integrations and to surface fidelity metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter can convert runtime-native streaming events into the OpenAI Responses event sequence with >99.5% token-order parity across our test corpus
Function-call sequences (start/arg/complete) are emitted in a way that matches OpenAI semantics for 95% of edge-case prompts (see tests) and produces a clear degradation event when lossy
Integration test harness (fixture set) that reproduces 25 representative parity gaps runs in CI and fails on regressions
Metrics: emit per-request fidelity score, delta-count, and latency overhead; surface in Console dashboard under Responses -> Parity
Canary plan executed: 5% traffic behind a toggle for two business days with automatic rollback on fidelity < 90% or error increase > 0.5%
implementation_notes: Design an observer module that attaches to the runtime event bus and writes an ordered event log (idempotent, append-only) with timing metadata
Create a reconciliation layer that consumes the event log and yields canonical 'response' events matching OpenAI semantics (choices.delta, choices.finish, tool_call.start/args/end)
Define lossiness taxonomy and a small set of deterministic heuristics (buffering windows, token reassembly, event coalescing) to resolve common mismatches
Add flags: adapter.mode = {strict, permissive, replayable}; strict enforces exact parity and fails fast, permissive applies heuristics, replayable stores events for postmortem replay
Add lightweight in-band fidelity markers in the response stream when a heuristic modified ordering or dropped metadata (clients can opt-out of markers)
Instrument counters: events_emitted, events_reconciled, heuristics_applied, tokens_reordered, functioncall_truncations
Benchmark added latency on p50/p95 for common sequence lengths; aim for <10ms p50 overhead on typical small completions and <50ms p95 on longer multi-tool sequences
Testing: extend existing responses-interop test corpus with 25 new fuzz cases (edge stops, interleaved tool calls, partial args) and add golden output files
Docs: update API compat guide in Confluence + example SDK snippet showing adapter toggle usage and interpretation of fidelity markers
